name: protobuf_peek
description: Read the wire structure of a protobuf message without its schema: for each field its number, wire type, absolute byte offset and full field-number path (3.1.2), with nested messages unwrapped. WIRE STRUCTURE, NOT MEANING: no field name, unit, enum or signedness is known without the .proto file; a top-level varint is returned raw with its zigzag reading (and its two's-complement reading where the top bit is set), a length-delimited field is a guess between a nested message, text and bytes (read_as, with also_reads_as for the other readings it could be). A message is checked as the encoding defines it: a varint is at most ten bytes, a field number is 1 to 536870911, wire types 6 and 7 do not exist, and a field that runs past its message is an error with its offset; a group (wire types 3 and 4, deprecated) stops the parse there and the window is not shown. consistent_with_protobuf_wire_format means the whole window parsed, which a short or ordinary blob can do by chance. SENSITIVE: a string or bytes field can hold message text or a credential, so the answer prints a top-level varint and nothing else that holds a value: not the text of a string, not the bytes of a bytes field, not a number under a length-delimited field (the bytes of a string or token now and then parse as a nested message, and their numbers are its content), not a fixed-width value (raw bytes); each has its offset, length and reading and a finding id. A length-delimited field whose bytes are printable text is text, never a nested message (a nested reading of a string would show its characters as field numbers, wire types and lengths); any other is read as a nested message only when it parses whole, has at least two fields, writes every varint in its shortest form, orders its field numbers ascending and keeps them at 300 or below (random bytes pass about once in 3,400; real Biome messages 17,871 times in 17,872), and is not entirely printable text. A binary value that does parse that way shows that structure, derived from its bytes (rare for a key or a token, not impossible), with its numbers withheld; its payload as a whole is written to the values file on request (kind bytes, with payload_offset), so nobody needs to aim a window at it. A window is held to the same rule, and to a stricter one when it was aimed (an offset past the start, or a length): it must then be at least 16 bytes with at least four fields, because the first answer names where each withheld payload is and a window slid across a token would otherwise print the token's characters as keys, lengths and varints. Rows, field numbers and varints are printed only for a window that meets the rule; any other window gets one status, not_accepted, in the same words whatever it was (a parse error, a group, text, too short, unordered), and NO COUNT: field_count, top_level_fields and counts are zero, since the parse stops at the first error and how many fields it read, how many were varints or nested, and how deep it went come from the window's bytes (a window slid over a token gave about two bits a character through them). Its bytes are in the values file on request, as one row of kind window (the whole window as hexadecimal, and what the parser found in a fixed width), so the file's size is the window's and not the parse's. A residual remains in the windows that are shown: on tokens that are the whole of one string field, a window slid across the token was shown for 13 to 99 percent of 12- to 64-character tokens under the plain rule and gave away 3 to 20 percent of a token's characters; under this rule 0 to 1.2 percent of tokens have such a window and at most 0.2 percent of a token's characters are derivable from it, never a whole token. The rule is tuned to that layout and is weaker outside it: a 32-character hexadecimal token split across two string fields had a shown window for 4.8 percent of tokens (0.8 percent of characters derivable), a 64-character hexadecimal token written as repeated six-byte pieces for 12.5 percent (1.1 percent), a 32-byte token as repeated six-byte pieces for 8.1 percent (0.5 percent), a 64-character hexadecimal token inside a nested message for 3.9 percent (0.4 percent); never a whole token in any of them. These rates hold at any max_fields: a window the field budget stopped is shown only when nobody aimed it (with max_fields 4 an aimed window was judged on its first four fields, and 19.1 percent of 64-character hexadecimal tokens had a shown window, 6.0 percent of 32-character ones and 1.2 percent of 24-character base62 ones; it is now 1.0, 0.6 and 0.1 percent, the same as at the default). What the values file's size follows: bytes, nested payloads, numbers and windows are written in a width the answer shows, but the text of a string field is written as JSON writes it, so a quote or a backslash adds a byte and a control or non-ASCII character adds more; a caller who isolates a field with offset and length reads about log2(count+1) bits of that field's quote, backslash and control-character count from the size of one call, and nothing from a token of letters and digits. The text is written readable on purpose, so this is stated and not removed. Nor is the time of the parse of a window that is not shown: it stops at the first error, so the job's duration says roughly how many fields were read before it (microseconds a field). Those values are written only on write_values: true, in a job run with secret_output: true, to $OUT/protobuf-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, refused if it exists; refused outside a job). WHAT A REQUESTING AGENT CAN SEE. The answer, and the job's file list with each file's size and digest, are what a requester is shown without asking. The values file is sealed under store/ of the sandbox, which an agent's VM mounts read-only: an agent that opens it reads every row, the values (and match) included. The measures above protect what is shown without anyone opening the file (the answer, its status and counts, the size and digest); they do not stop an agent that deliberately opens the sealed file, and this tool does not decide whether it may (that is the sandbox's mounts). hex puts the message in the call, and a call is recorded in the trace: use a path for anything that may be sensitive (hex is limited to 64 KiB). Only a bounded window is read (length, default 8 MiB, at most 64 MiB): what lies past it is counted and next_offset says where to continue. Memory follows the window, not its depth. Budgets: max_depth (default 6, at most 32), max_fields including those tried as a nested message (default 100000, at most 500000) and max_seconds (default 60, at most 90); a budget that ends the parse is reported (partial, with resume_offset where to continue), and fields the depth budget kept from being tried as nested messages are counted (fields_not_tried_as_nested_at_max_depth), never silent. A path that is not a regular file (a named pipe) is refused. There is no universal protobuf signature, so this tool declares no automatic file match. STATUS: complete only when the window parsed whole as a message under the acceptance rule AND nothing lies after it (window.bytes_after_window is 0); a window that is not the whole input is partial whatever it parsed as (structure.status and structure.consistent_with_protobuf_wire_format stay about the window, and window.next_offset says where the next window starts), as is a parse that a budget or the clock stopped and a window that is not accepted.

path.description: A file holding one protobuf message (or a message at `offset` in it)

hex.description: The message as hexadecimal instead of a file (at most 64 KiB; the call, and so the message, is recorded in the trace)

offset.description: Start decoding at this byte offset of the file (offsets in the answer are absolute)

length.description: Bytes to decode from offset (default: up to 8 MiB; at most 64 MiB); the answer says what lies after the window

max_depth.description: How deep to try fields as nested messages (default 6, at most 32)

max_fields.description: Fields to parse, tentative nested readings included (default 100000, at most 500000); a window you aimed (offset or length) that this budget stopped is not shown, so a small value hides more and never shows more

max_seconds.description: Stop parsing after this long (default 60, at most 90)

limit.description: Fields in the inline answer (default 200, and at most 1 MiB of rows); the whole list is in the file the answer names

write_values.description: Write the text of string fields, the hexadecimal of bytes fields and of the payload of a field read as a nested message, the numbers under a length-delimited field (padded to one width), and, for a window that was not accepted, the whole window as hexadecimal with what the parser found, to $OUT/protobuf-values.jsonl (default false). Every row carries a random run id. Refused unless the tool runs as a job, which must be run with secret_output: true; the answer never carries them
